question: A conducting rod of length $0.60\text{ m}$ moves at right angles to a uniform magnetic field of $0.40\text{ T}$ with a speed of $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the emf induced across the ends of the rod. How will the emf change if the length of the rod is halved? Justify your answer.

options.A:
The induced emf is $0.36\text{ V}$.
If the length is halved, the emf becomes $0.72\text{ V}$.
options.B:
The induced emf is $0.72\text{ V}$.
If the length is halved, the emf remains unchanged.
options.C:
The induced emf is $0.72\text{ V}$.
Since $\varepsilon=Blv$, halving the length halves the emf to $0.36\text{ V}$.
options.D:
The induced emf is $1.44\text{ V}$.
If the length is halved, the emf becomes $0.72\text{ V}$.
